signals: Proposed label: the_priced_out_beginner. A 20-year-old bar back with essentially no budget — 'Pretty much free, almost' — who is already getting good results from the provider's free content and wants structure rather than rescue.

None of the existing labels fit. He is not the_optimizer: no income, no success to build on, and price was an absolute barrier rather than a quality signal. He is not skeptical_bargain_hunter: he is not sceptical and has no cheap competitor anchor, he simply has no money. He is not the_rebuilder or the_preserver: at 20 with visible abs and no injuries there is nothing to rebuild or preserve.
His actual problem is nutritional, not motivational — 'I want to eat more, and I try to eat more, but my appetite just isn't there'

Eat more consistently and enough to grow, despite a low appetite

objections.raw_quote: I mean, both. Depends on how much the actual course is because a lot of money you can't afford that.
objections.rep_response: Disclosed immediately that one-to-one with Trevor is 'at least in the four figures', read the prospect's reaction on camera, and asked what budget he had in mind.

objections.raw_quote: Not a lot. But it can be 10 bucks... Pretty much free, almost.
objections.rep_response: Named the cheapest available option at $200 a month, checked the reaction directly — 'do you feel like, whoa, that's just way too much for me?' — accepted the yes, and redirected him to Trevor's free YouTube content with an offer to stay in touch.

evidence: The prospect ruled himself out on the one-to-one before a price was even given: 'I'm out on that one.'
He confirmed that the cheapest tier was also out of reach — asked 'do you feel like, whoa, that's just way too much for me?' he answered 'Yeah.'
The rep disqualified rather than discounted, and redirected him to free content: 'I really advise you if you're not looking to really invest that much into it at the moment yet, which I understand.'
No payment, no link, no next call. The only follow-up is a YouTube link and an open door: 'you always have my number as well, so you can always just hit me up.'
Counter-evidence: the relationship was left warm and the rep offered to stay in contact, so a future conversation is plausible — but nothing was agreed and no timeline exists.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send Trevor's YouTube channel; prospect to continue self-directed and contact the rep if his position changes.

notable.note: The cleanest call in the batch on conduct. Faced with a 20-year-old bar back with no budget, the rep disclosed the price band early, asked the budget question directly, accepted the answer, declined to discount, and sent him to free content — the opposite of the pattern on the other calls in this folder, where an unaffordable price was answered by inventing a cheaper tier. Two things still stand out: the $200/month Primal University price is quoted again as though it were a standard rung on the ladder, and the prospect's actual problem — under-eating at 150 lb with an absent appetite and long-standing picky eating — was identified and then left entirely unexplored.

The same happens across the budget exchange at 00:08:42 to 00:08:57, where 'I'm out on that one' and 'Pretty much free, almost' are correctly the prospect's but the questions between them are misattributed.
